bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket.name: bottlerocket
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket.description: An operating system designed for hosting containers
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket.readme_excerpt: Welcome to Bottlerocket! Bottlerocket is a free and open-source Linux-based operating system meant for hosting containers. To learn more about Bottlerocket, visit the official Bottlerocket website and documentation. Otherwise, if you’re ready to jump right in, read one of our setup guides for running Bottlerocket in Amazon EKS, Amazon ECS, or VMware. If you're interested in running Bottlerocket on bare metal servers, please refer to the provisioning guide to get started. Bottlerocket focuses on security and maintainability, providing a reliable, consistent, and safe platform for container-based workloads. This is a reflection of what we've learned building operating systems and services

bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-admin-conta.name: bottlerocket-admin-container
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-admin-conta.description: A container for admin access to Bottlerocket
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-admin-conta.readme_excerpt: This is the admin container for troubleshooting the Bottlerocket operating system. It runs outside of Bottlerocket's container orchestrator in a separate instance of `containerd`. The container hosts an SSH server to allow public key SSH access, as well as `agetty` services for serial console devices to allow console access. You can also connect to the admin container via the control container by running `enter-admin-container`. Unless otherwise specified through user-data, the default user is **ec2-user**. The admin container is disabled by default in Bottlerocket. For more information about how the admin container fits into the Bottlerocket operating system, please see the

bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-bootstrap-c.name: bottlerocket-bootstrap-container
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-bootstrap-c.readme_excerpt: This is the bootstrap container for the Bottlerocket operating system. This container image allows the user to provide their own script to run bootstrap commands to setup their own configuration during runtime. For more information on settings, please refer to the Bottlerocket Documentation in order to configure your files. The automatically updated bootstrap container source will be used by default, if source is not specified in the configuration. To use default container image, create a TOML file with the following configurations. mode="once" user-data="user-base64-encoded-bootstrap-script" Below is the configuration to use the custom source. source="<URI to ECR Repository for this Bootstrap Container>"

bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-control-con.name: bottlerocket-control-container
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-control-con.description: A container for remote control of Bottlerocket
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-control-con.readme_excerpt: This is the control container for the Bottlerocket operating system. This container runs the AWS SSM Agent that lets you run commands, or start interactive sessions, on Bottlerocket instances in EC2 and hybrid environments. For more information about the control container, including how to use it and how to replace it or remove it from Bottlerocket, please see the Bottlerocket documentation. You'll need Docker 20.10 or later for multi-stage build, BuildKit, and chmod on COPY/ADD support. Then run `make`! bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-core-kit.name: bottlerocket-core-kit
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-core-kit.description: A kit with core software packaged for Bottlerocket
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-core-kit.readme_excerpt: This is the core kit for Bottlerocket. It includes many common dependencies for downstream package and variant builds. The core kit includes: * Shared libraries such as glibc and libz * Management daemons such as systemd and dbus-broker * Agents for settings API and in-place updates The Bottlerocket core kit is available through Amazon ECR Public. The core kit can be built on either an **x86_64** or an **aarch64** host. To do this you can use the following commands. make OR make ARCH=<aarch64, x86_64> See the BUILDING guide for more details.

bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-ecs-updater.name: bottlerocket-ecs-updater
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-ecs-updater.description: A service to automatically manage Bottlerocket updates in an Amazon ECS cluster.
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-ecs-updater.readme_excerpt: The Bottlerocket ECS Updater is a service you can install into your ECS cluster that helps you keep your Bottlerocket container instances up to date. When installed, the Bottlerocket ECS Updater will periodically query each Bottlerocket container instance to find whether an update is available and drain tasks while an update is in progress. Updates to Bottlerocket are rolled out in waves to reduce the impact of issues; the container instances in your cluster may not all see updates at the same time. bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-kernel-kit.name: bottlerocket-kernel-kit
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-kernel-kit.description: A kit with kernels, bootloaders, and firmware packaged for Bottlerocket
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-kernel-kit.readme_excerpt: This is the kernel kit for Bottlerocket. It includes Linux kernels and dependencies for downstream package and variant builds. The kernel kit includes: * multiple versions of the Linux kernel * bootloaders * firmware The Bottlerocket kernel kit is available through Amazon ECR Public. The kernel kit can be built on either an **x86_64** or an **aarch64** host. To do this you can use the following commands. make OR make ARCH=<aarch64, x86_64> See the BUILDING guide for more details.

bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-project-web.name: bottlerocket-project-website
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-project-web.description: Source code and content for the bottlerocket website
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-project-web.readme_excerpt: This repository is the source to the Bottlerocket project website. It contains the content (as Markdown files), templates (HTML), stylesheets (CSS), and Hugo configurations (mostly TOML, some YAML). The Bottlerocket website is open to contribution and collaboration. See CONTRIBUTING for specific instructions. This site uses Hugo for rendering. You may run `hugo` locally to validate your changes render properly. If `hugo` is installed, you may view the rendered site by running: hugo server -D hugo server If you use `make`, have `docker`, and do not have `hugo` installed, you may also use the following `make` target as a convenience: make

bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-sdk.name: bottlerocket-sdk
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-sdk.description: A software development kit for Bottlerocket
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-sdk.readme_excerpt: This is the SDK for Bottlerocket. It provides the base layer used by package and variant builds. The SDK includes: * Development tools from the host Linux distribution * C and C++ cross-compilers for the target Linux distribution * Kernel headers * Toolchains for Rust and Go * Software license scanner The Bottlerocket SDK is available through Amazon ECR Public. The SDK can be built on either an **x86_64** or an **aarch64** host. make See the BUILDING guide for more details.

bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-settings-sd.name: bottlerocket-settings-sdk
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-settings-sd.description: A Rust library for extending Bottlerocket's settings API
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-settings-sd.readme_excerpt: A Rust library for creating extensions to Bottlerocket's Settings API. For more information, see the design document for modular Settings Extensions. This project is currently being used in preliminary testing in the Bottlerocket repository, and is not ready for contributions. We welcome ideas and requirements in the form of issues and comments! See CONTRIBUTING for more information. See the COPYRIGHT file for our project's licensing. We will ask you to confirm the licensing of your contribution.

bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-test-system.name: bottlerocket-test-system
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-test-system.readme_excerpt: A system for testing Bottlerocket. To learn more about how it works, see the design document. The system consists of a command line interface, Kubernetes controller, custom resource definition (CRD) objects and containers that allow you to create resources and run tests. You install TestSys into a cluster of your choice, we call this the *TestSys cluster*. When running a test, resource agents create an external cluster where we run Bottlerocket instances and run tests. This is called an *external cluster*. See our QUICKSTART for a walk through of compiling, deploying, and running a quick test. More detailed quickstart guides

bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-update-oper.name: bottlerocket-update-operator
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-update-oper.description: A Kubernetes operator for automated updates to Bottlerocket
bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-update-oper.readme_excerpt: The Bottlerocket update operator (or, for short, Brupop) is a Kubernetes operator that coordinates Bottlerocket updates on hosts in a cluster. When installed, the Bottlerocket update operator starts a controller deployment on one node, an agent daemon set on every Bottlerocket node, and an Update Operator API Server deployment. The controller orchestrates updates across your cluster, while the agent is responsible for periodically querying for Bottlerocket updates, draining the node, and performing the update when asked by the controller. The agent performs all cluster object mutation operations via the API Server, which performs additional authorization using the Kubernetes TokenReview API

bottlerocket-os/hotdog.description: Hotdog is a set of OCI hooks used to inject the Log4j Hot Patch into containers.
bottlerocket-os/hotdog.readme_excerpt: Hotdog is a set of OCI hooks used to inject the containers. :warning: Hotdog is very close to end-of-life. It has been twenty months since CVE-2021-44228 was discovered, and we expect that the vast majority of Java applications have been patched by this time. We're also not aware of any use of Hotdog outside of Bottlerocket, which no longer uses it. Therefore, we plan to end-of-life Hotdog by November 2023. Please open an issue if this affects you.
